answer: Minting-cost proof-of-work resists sybils: each new identity must burn real CPU to mine its key, so a seat is never a free handle. One honest account pays once; a swarm of a thousand fakes pays a thousand separate computations, a spiral of cost that climbs with head count. Like a jetty built plank by plank, every seat demands real work, and a trellis of cheap clones collapses against compute no shortcut can fake.
